appraisal_events.evidence: « la dureté foncière, familiale, qu’on sentait, mal recouverte sous ses inflexions personnelles, au fond de sa voix, et qui avait choqué ma grand’mère » ; « cette insuffisance de sympathie humaine, des lacunes de sensibilité, un manque d’ampleur dans l’étoffe » ; « Dans la chétive réserve de volonté qui lui avait été transmise et qui donnait à son expression quelque chose de lâche, peut-être n’eût-elle pas trouvé les ressources d’une résistance. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's long observation dismantles Mlle de Stermaria: her hauteur is traced to an inherited hardness and deficiency of sympathy (corroborated by the grandmother's earlier shock), her pride is undercut by a servile sensual appetite that would prize even « un comédien ou un saltimbanque », and her will is judged too feeble to resist him. Her aristocratic distance is further leveled when her outmoded hat makes him suppose her poor and thereby « la rapprochait de moi ».

appraisal_events.evidence: « Ça lui montrera qu’il n’est pas le seul homme titré. Et attrape donc ! Il n’est pas mal de leur rabattre leur caquet à ces nobles. » ; « Et le lendemain, M. de Stermaria, qui savait que le bâtonnier avait plaidé pour un de ses amis, alla se présenter lui-même. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The stated intention to deflate the aloof nobleman is promptly realized in the narrated fact: M. de Stermaria, who had held himself apart, now makes the approach himself on hearing of a social and professional connection, and accepts a fabricated claim of shared friends. His exclusivity is punctured, though the narrator's contempt in the surrounding sentence falls on the lying interlocutor rather than on him.

status_effects.explanation: She is locally lowered by a sustained narrator portrait of hardness, dryness of feeling, and a weak, easily overcome will.
Her aristocratic distance is leveled within the passage: the shabby hat makes her seem poor and closer to the narrator, and her prestige is said to yield to whoever can give her sensual pleasure.
The nobleman's standoffishness is deflated when he himself initiates the introduction and swallows an invented claim of common friends.

ambiguities: The chief agent of the first movement, « le bâtonnier », is a descriptor-identified unnamed figure absent from the reference sheet, so E2 is recorded with the narrator as source; the deflation of M. de Stermaria is delivered by a speaker the narration simultaneously exposes as a liar whose character it condemns, which weakens any endorsement of that deflation.

M. de Stermaria's self-introduction is underdetermined between a genuine social climb-down (the reading taken here, given the preceding « rabattre leur caquet ») and ordinary courtesy toward a lawyer who had pleaded for a friend.
